Thanks again for the deep dive earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned on SLOs and validation plan: 

Summary of SLOs you confirmed on the call:
- 95th percentile latency (token streaming): <= 220ms
- Sustained throughput: 1500 concurrent tokens/sec (mixed prompt sizes)
- Peak concurrency: 120 concurrent requests (avg request ~200 tokens)
- Streaming requirement: low-latency incremental token flush (<= 50ms flush cadence)

Questions / Items we promised to follow up on:
1) GPU sizing recommendations for Dedicated (A100 vs H100 vs L4) — Rafael will propose configurations and reserved throughput.
2) Validation plan: synthetic load patterns that mimic your production mix + two-week soak test.
3) Attachments: I shared a performance matrix (acme_performance_matrix.xlsx) and a draft SLA (redwood_sla_draft.pdf) — see attached.

Proposed next steps:
- Rafael to send sizing options and estimated reserved throughput by EOD Monday (11/23).
- We’ll provision a 2-week POC with monitoring dashboards and token-level cost breakdown.
- Joint runbook for fallback/overflow routing if Dedicated capacity reaches headroom.

If this aligns, I’ll schedule the POC kickoff for the week of 11/30.

Thanks —

Hi Sam —

Attached are three recommended configurations (high-level) for Dedicated capacity to meet your SLOs. I’ve included expected reserved throughput (tokens/sec), expected 95th latency estimates (token streaming) and cost banding. See acme_performance_matrix.xlsx for the table; key highlights below.

Option A — H100 (best perf, higher cost)
- Provision: 4 x H100-80GB (NVL) in a single pool with continuous batching and KV cache enabled
- Reserved throughput: ~5,500 tokens/sec aggregate
- Expected 95th latency (streaming): ~140-180ms under mixed load
- Peak concurrency headroom: comfortably handles 200 concurrent requests with avg 200 tokens
- Notes: best for aggressive latency SLOs and future growth.

Option B — A100 (balanced)
- Provision: 6 x A100-80GB in pool
- Reserved throughput: ~4,000 tokens/sec aggregate
- Expected 95th latency: ~180-240ms depending on sequence length distribution
- Peak concurrency: ~140 concurrent requests (avg 200 tokens) before queuing begins
- Notes: cost-effective mid-tier; may need autoscaled burst to H100 for spikes.

Option C — L4 (cost-optimized for short form streaming)
- Provision: 12 x L4 (or equivalent M60 series)
- Reserved throughput: ~2,200 tokens/sec aggregate
- Expected 95th latency: ~200-300ms (short prompt workloads are favorable)
- Peak concurrency: ~90 concurrent requests
- Notes: best for majority-short prompt workloads; long-form and high concurrency will stretch it.

Sizing recommendation for Acme (based on your mix and target SLOs): Option B as baseline with an H100-backed burst reserve (hybrid pool) to protect p95 latency during peaks. That maps to an initial commit sized to ~4k tokens/sec with a 20-30% burst capacity.

Validation plan (high level):
- Week 1: Provision baseline (Option B) and run synthetic mixes that mirror your 70/30 distribution. Collect token-level latency histograms, KV cache hit rate, and streaming flush cadence metrics.
- Week 2: Increase concurrency to peak target (120) and run soak tests; exercise failure/fallback routing.
- Deliverable: performance runbook + monitoring dashboard + cost/latency trade-off sheet.

Attachments included: acme_performance_matrix.xlsx (detailed numbers), redwood_sla_draft.pdf (SLA draft).

-Rafael
